question: LCM and HCF of two numbers are 198 and 9 respectively. If one of the numbers is 99, then find the other number.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the property: First Number × Second Number = LCM × HCF

99 × Second Number = 198 × 9

Second Number = (198 × 9) ÷ 99

Second Number = 2 × 9 = 18

**∴ The correct answer is 18.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

LCM of two numbers = 198

HCF of two numbers = 9

First Number = 99

**Formula Used:**

First Number × Second Number = LCM × HCF

**Calculations:**

⇒ 99 × Second Number = 198 × 9

⇒ Second Number = (198 × 9) ÷ 99

⇒ Second Number = 198 ÷ 99 × 9

⇒ Second Number = 2 × 9

⇒ Second Number = 18

**∴ The correct answer is 18.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relation between LCM and HCF

The product of the LCM and HCF of any two given natural numbers is strictly equal to the product of the given numbers. The formula is: LCM × HCF = N₁ × N₂.

HCF and LCM of Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are called co-prime if their HCF is exactly 1. Because of this, the LCM of two co-prime numbers will always be their direct product.

LCM and HCF of Fractions

LCM of fractions = LCM of Numerators ÷ HCF of Denominators.
HCF of fractions = HCF of Numerators ÷ LCM of Denominators.
